items.readable_text:
Content:
To multiply a two-digit number by a one-digit number, we can use the standard algorithm.

Content:
For example, to multiply [MATH: 23] by [MATH: 3,] we write the two-digit number above the one-digit number, lining up the place values:

Content:
[MATH: 2|3; ×|3|48 + 720 = 76800000000]

Content:
First, we multiply the ones, placing the answer in the ones column under the line:

Content:
[MATH: _(0); 2|3; ×|3; 9|3 × 3 = 90000000000000000; Write:9]

Content:
Then, we multiply by the value in the tens place, putting the answer in the tens column under the line:

Content:
[MATH: _(0); 2|3; ×|3; 6|9|2 × 3 = 60000000000000000; Write:6]

Content:
Therefore, [MATH: 23 \times 3 = 69.]

Content:
Sometimes when multiplying the ones, the result is two digits long.

Content:
In this case, we write down the digit in the ones place, and we carry the digit in the tens place. We then add the carried digit to the result of the multiplication of the tens.

Content:
For example, let's multiply [MATH: 26] by [MATH: 6.]

Content:
[MATH: 2|6; ×|6|14and3 + 14 = 170000]

Content:
First, we multiply the ones. We have [MATH: 6\times6= {\color{blue}3}{\color{red}6}], so we write the ones place value, [MATH: \color{red}6], and carry the tens place value, [MATH: {\color{blue}3}\mathbin{:}]

Content:
[MATH: _(3); 2|6; ×|6; 6|6 × 6 = 3600000000000000000; Carry:3; Write:6]

Content:
Finally, we multiply the tens. We have [MATH: 2\times 6 = 12], to which we add the carry of [MATH: {\color{blue}3}\mathbin{:}]

Content:
[MATH: _(3); 2|6; ×|6; 1|5|6|2 × 6 = 12and3 + 12 = 15; Carry:−; Write:15]

Content:
When we reach the tens multiplication, we do not carry anything. Instead, we write down the complete result.

Content:
Therefore, [MATH: 26 \times 6 = 156.]

sections.normalized_html: Calculate [MATH: 37\times 4.]

We write it this way:

[MATH: 3|7; ×|4|3 × 4 = 12and2 + 12 = 14]

First, we multiply the ones:

[MATH: _(2); 3|7; ×|4; 8|7 × 4 = 28and2 + 12 = 14; Carry:2; Write:8]

Finally, we multiply the tens:

[MATH: _(2); 3|7; ×|4; 1|4|8|3 × 4 = 12and2 + 12 = 14; Carry:−; Write:14]

Therefore, [MATH: 37 \times 4 = 148.]
